Definition: Baali, a symbolical name for Jehovah
BiblicalUsage: Baali is the name Hosea says Israel will stop using for God — in that day thou shalt call me Ishi, and shalt call me no more Baali — and the word means my master, which God says is too close to the name of the false god to keep. A new name for a new covenant: my husband, not my master.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that God cares about the names we call him, and Baali had to go because it sounded like Baal. He wants Ishi — husband — and that tells me what the covenant really is.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
